replay.binding: same call identities, current observed signatures

external_invariants: FP32 weights and features (workloads.json dtype float32); TF32 disabled via torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False, and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest') (infer.py:13-18; adapter.py:60-64).

Model architecture is fixed: two-layer mean GraphSAGE GraphEncoder with input_features=128, hidden_features=256, output_features=64, ReLU between layers, each layer projecting concat(self features, mean neighbor features) with nn.Linear (model.py; adapter.py:33-53).
model.eval() plus forward under @torch.inference_mode(); no cross-invocation state (infer.py:18,28-30; adapter.py:65,90-92).

Seeded fixtures reproduced exactly: torch.manual_seed(20261021) before model construction; a CPU torch.Generator seeded 20271021 (seed+1) produces features = randn(nodes, 128), sources = randint(nodes, (edges,)), destinations = randint(nodes, (edges,)); degree = torch.bincount(destinations, minlength=nodes).float(); for this request's workload nodes=7168 and edges=143360, i.e. features [7168, 128], sources/destinations [143360] and degree [7168] (infer.py:14-25, workloads.json seed; adapter.py:61,66-74).

Graph semantics: duplicate directed edges contribute individually via index_add_ on a zeros_like base; nodes without incoming edges keep zero neighbor features; neighbor mean divides by degree.clamp_min(1).unsqueeze(1) (model.py:11-15, README.md:17-19; adapter.py:38-42).

Quality check: the complete FP32 output tensor (shape [nodes, output_features] = [7168, 64] for the unseen_graph workload of this request) compared with torch.testing.assert_close(atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4); output is continuous floating point with no discrete outputs (infer.py:44-45, workloads.json quality; request.json quality).

One run() equals exactly one model(features, sources, destinations, degree) forward on GPU-resident tensors (adapter.py:90-92, mirroring infer.py:28-30); the full workload must be executed even though the objective is a single latency number.

Workload dimensions (nodes=7168, edges=143360) are read from request['workload'] in prepare(), not embedded as constants (adapter.py:59,67-74); this request measures the unseen_graph workload (the workloads.json held_out_workloads entry, README.md:21-22), which the frozen adapter executes unchanged because nodes and edges are parameterized from the request.
Single-process, single-device workload: model and inputs live on context['device']; no distributed backend and no communication (request devices/communication).

Goal and metric scope (request.json): minimize latency_ms (unit ms) for one full graph encoder forward on the unseen_graph workload (7168 nodes, 143360 edges), preserving the full output checks; the objective has no constraints, and the workloads.json peak_allocated_bytes goal with its graphs_per_second >= 0.95 baseline_ratio constraint is not part of this request; graphs_per_second = 1000/latency_ms, nodes, edges and peak_allocated_bytes are recorded sample metrics only (workloads.json goals; adapter.py:99-109).

Measurement policy: latency_ms is wall-clock time around one forward with torch.cuda.synchronize on both sides of the completion boundary (infer.py:53-58); measurement_lifetime is per invocation with warmup=3 and repeats=15 and a statistics.median summary mirroring infer.py:49-63 (request.json); peak_allocated_bytes comes from torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() queried outside the timer after the post-run synchronization (infer.py:59-60; adapter.py:107-108).

Frozen adapter state protocol (executes this request unchanged): prepare(context, request) reproduces infer.py:12-25 outside timing — torch.set_num_threads(4), seeding, TF32 disabled, float32_matmul_precision('highest'), GraphEncoder(128, 256, 64) built on CPU then moved to context['device'] and eval'd, CPU-generator fixture then moved to the device, nodes and edges from request['workload'] (adapter.py:56-83); reset(state) is a no-op because inference has no cross-invocation state (adapter.py:86-88); observe(state, result) returns the complete detached output tensor on CPU (adapter.py:95-96); models(state) exposes the loaded GraphEncoder root module for discovery/replacement (adapter.py:112-113); set_mode records the mode and execution is identical in quality/measure/profile because the full output is always produced (adapter.py:116-118).
